metrics.dC: candidate spent bytes minus comparator spent bytes per scene (negative is cheaper)
metrics.dY: candidate on-time tasks minus comparator on-time tasks per scene (positive is better)

predicates.joint_dominant: dY >= 0 and dC <= 0 and not (dY == 0 and dC == 0)

resampling.shared_by: every task and cost comparison of this round
resampling.unit: the 64 scenes are the paired sampling unit; 192 launches are not 192 independent scenes

section: pre-registered statistics plan (frozen before the first launch)
single_reader: tables, judgement and verdict read the one machine-readable statistics artefact (PAIRED_COMPARISON.json); no second sampling is performed
stopping: none of these criteria stops the batch mid-run; only technical health and the launch quota decide stopping

verdict_fields.observed_task_count_status: no_observed_count_loss only when dY >= 0 in every scene against BOTH comparators
verdict_fields.primary_cost_evidence: lower_cost_supported only when the primary dC 95% CI upper bound < 0; otherwise lower_cost_not_established

zero_event_rule: when zero net task degradations are observed against a comparator, attach 1-0.05^(1/64) (~4.57%) as the single-sided 95% upper bound on the per-scenario probability of a degradation event under an i.i.d. assumption; it is not an expected task-loss bound and not a deployment guarantee
